explanation: The September 2018 FOMC document contains substantive policy content that could plausibly explain a market break on October 11: the removal of the word 'accommodative' from the policy statement signaled that the Fed no longer viewed policy as easy, combined with a rate hike to 2-2.25% and increased balance sheet runoff caps taking effect in October ($30B Treasury/$20B MBS), all of which tightened financial conditions and could have contributed to the sharp equity selloff and yield spike observed around that date.
